paragraphs.sourceText: Why Are Asian Americans Missing from Our Textbooks?
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么亚裔美国人从我们的教科书中消失了？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) I still remember my fourth-grade social studies project. Our class was studying the Gold Rush, something all California fourth-graders learned. I was excited because I had asked to research Chinese immigrants during that era. Growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area, I had always known that "San Francisco" translated to "Gold Mountain" in Chinese. The name had stuck ever since Chinese immigrants arrived on the shores of Northern California in the 1850s, eager to try their luck in the gold mines. Now l'd have the chance to learn about them.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 我仍然记得我四年级的社会研究项目。我们班正在研究淘金热，这是所有加州四年级学生都学到的东西。我很兴奋，因为我要求研究那个时代的中国移民。我在旧金山湾区长大，一直知道“旧金山”中文翻译为“金山”。自从 1850 年代中国移民抵达北加州海岸，渴望在金矿里碰碰运气以来，这个名字就一直沿用至今。现在我有机会了解他们了。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) My excitement was short-lived. I remember heading to the library with my class and asking for help. I remember the librarian's hesitation. She finally led me past row after row of books, to a corner of the library where she pulled an oversized book off the shelf. She checked the index and turned over to a page about early Chinese immigrants in California. That was all there was in my entire school library in San Francisco, home of the nation's first Chinatown. That was it.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 我的兴奋是短暂的。我记得和全班同学一起去图书馆寻求帮助。我记得图书管理员的犹豫。她终于领着我穿过一排又一排的书，来到图书馆的一个角落，从书架上取下一本超大的书。她查了一下索引，翻到了关于早期加州华人移民的页面。这就是我位于旧金山的整个学校图书馆的全部内容，旧金山是美国第一个唐人街的所在地。就是这样。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) I finally had the opportunity to learn about Asian Americans like myself, and how we became part of the fabric of the United States when I took an introductory class on Asian-American history in college. The class was a revelation. I realized how much had been missing in my textbooks as I grew up. My identity had been shaped by years of never reading, seeing, hearing, or learning about people who had a similar background as me. Why, I wondered, weren't the stories, histories, and contributions of Asian Americans taught in K-12 schools, especially in the elementary schools? Why are they still not taught?
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 当我在大学选修亚裔美国人历史入门课程时，我终于有机会了解像我这样的亚裔美国人，以及我们如何成为美国社会的一部分。这堂课是一个启示。在我的成长过程中，我意识到我的教科书中遗漏了多少东西。我的身份是由于多年来从未阅读、看到、听到或了解与我有相似背景的人而形成的。我想知道，为什么 K-12 学校，特别是小学没有教授亚裔美国人的故事、历史和贡献？为什么他们仍然没有被教导？

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Our students Asian, Latino, African American, Native American, and, yes, white stand to gain from a multicultural curriculum. Students of color are more engaged and earn better grades when they see themselves in their studies. Research has also found that white students benefit by being challenged and exposed to new perspectives.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 我们的亚洲学生、拉丁裔学生、非裔美国人、美洲原住民，当然还有白人学生都将从多元文化课程中获益。当有色人种学生在学习中看到自己时，他们会更加投入并取得更好的成绩。研究还发现，白人学生通过接受挑战和接触新观点而受益。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) For decades, activists have called for schools to offer anti-racism or multicultural curricula. Yet a traditional American K-12 curriculum continues to be taught from a Eurocentric point of view. Being multicultural often falls back on weaving children of color into photographs, or creating a few supporting characters that happen to be ethnic an improvement, but superficial nonetheless. Elementary school classrooms celebrate cultural holidays—Lunar New Year l Red envelopes l Lion dancers! —but they're quick to gloss over (掩饰）the challenges and injustices that Asian Americans have faced. Most students don't, for example, learn about the laws that for years excluded Asians from immigrating to the U.S. They don't hear the narratives of how and why Southeast Asian refugees （难民）had to rebuild their lives here.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 几十年来，活动人士一直呼吁学校提供反种族主义或多元文化课程。然而，传统的美国 K-12 课程仍然以欧洲为中心的观点进行教学。多元文化往往依赖于将有色人种的孩子编织到照片中，或者创造一些恰好是种族的配角，这是一种进步，但仍然很肤浅。小学教室庆祝文化节日——农历新年 l 红包 l 舞狮！ ——但他们很快就掩盖了亚裔美国人所面临的挑战和不公正。例如，大多数学生并没有了解多年来禁止亚裔移民到美国的法律。他们没有听到关于东南亚难民如何以及为何不得不在这里重建生活的叙述。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Research into what students learn in school has found just how much is missing in their studies. In an analysis, Christine Sleeter, a professor in the College of Professional Studies at California State University, Monterey Bay, reviewed California's history and social studies framework, the curriculum determined by state educators that influences what is taught in K-12 classrooms. Of the nearly 100 Americans recommended to be studied, 77% were white, 18% African American, 4% Native American, and 1 % Latino. None were Asian American.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 对学生在学校所学内容的研究发现他们的学习中到底缺失了多少内容。加州州立大学蒙特利湾分校专业研究学院教授 Christine Sleeter 在一项分析中回顾了加州的历史和社会研究框架，该框架是由州教育工作者确定的课程，影响着 K-12 课堂的教学内容。在建议研究的近 100 名美国人中，77% 是白人，18% 是非洲裔美国人，4% 是美洲原住民，1% 是拉丁裔。没有一个是亚裔美国人。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Worse, when Asian Americans do make an appearance in lesson books, it is often laced with problems. "There hasn't been much progress," says Nicholas Hartlep, an assistant professor at Metropolitan State University. His 2016 study of K-12 social studies textbooks and teacher manuals found that Asian Americans were poorly represented at best, and subjected to racist caricatures (拙劣 的模仿）at worst. The wide diversity of Asian Americans was overlooked; there was very little mention of South Asians or Pacific Islanders, for example. And chances were, in the images, Asian Americans appeared in stereotypical (模式化的）roles, such as engineers.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 更糟糕的是，当亚裔美国人确实出现在教科书中时，往往会遇到问题。 “并没有取得太大进展，”大都会州立大学助理教授尼古拉斯·哈特普说。他 2016 年对 K-12 社会研究教科书和教师手册的研究发现，亚裔美国人在最好的情况下代表性较差，在最坏的情况下受到种族主义漫画的影响。亚裔美国人的广泛多样性被忽视了；例如，很少提及南亚人或太平洋岛民。而且在图像中，亚裔美国人很可能出现在刻板的（模式化的）角色中，例如工程师。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Teachers with a multicultural background or training could perhaps overcome such curriculum challenges, but they're few and far between. In California, 65% of K-12 teachers are white, compared with a student population that is 75% students of color. Nationwide, the gap is even greater. It isn't a requirement that teachers share the same racial or ethnic background as their students, but the imbalance poses challenges, from the potential for unconscious bias to a lack of knowledge or comfort in discussing race and culture.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 具有多元文化背景或接受过培训的教师也许可以克服此类课程挑战，但这种情况很少见。在加利福尼亚州，65% 的 K-12 教师是白人，而学生群体中 75% 是有色人种学生。从全国来看，差距更大。教师并不要求与学生具有相同的种族或民族背景，但这种不平衡带来了挑战，从潜在的无意识偏见到在讨论种族和文化时缺乏知识或舒适度。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) How race and ethnicity is taught is crucial, says Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales, an Asian-American studies professor at San Francisco State University. She added that it's not so much about the teacher's background, but about training. "You can have a great curriculum but if you don't have teachers dedicated (专注于）to teaching it well," she says, "it won't work as well as you want it to."
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 旧金山州立大学亚裔美国人研究教授艾莉森·丁蒂昂科-库巴莱斯 (Allyson Tintiangco-Cubales) 表示，如何教授种族和族裔问题至关重要。她补充说，这与老师的背景无关，而是与培训有关。 “你可以拥有很棒的课程，但如果没有老师专注于教好它，”她说，“它就不会达到你想要的效果。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Some teachers are finding ways to expose students to Asian-American issues if not during school hours, then outside of them. This summer, Wilson Wong will lead a class of rising fifth-graders at a day camp dedicated to Chinese culture and the Chinese-American community in Oakland, California. His students, for instance, will learn about how Chinese immigrants built the railroads in California, and even have a chance to "experience" it themselves: They will race each other to build a railroad model on the playground, with some students being forced to "work" longer and faster and at cheaper wages. Wong, a middle school teacher during the school year, hopes he's exposing the students to how Chinese Americans contributed to the U.S., something that he didn't get as a student growing up in the San Francisco Bay Area. "I planted the seeds early," he says. "That's what I'm hoping for."
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 一些老师正在想方设法让学生接触亚裔美国人的问题，如果不在上课时间，那就在课外。今年夏天，威尔逊·黄将带领一群五年级新生参加位于加利福尼亚州奥克兰的一个致力于中国文化和美籍华人社区的日间夏令营。例如，他的学生将了解中国移民如何在加州建造铁路，甚至有机会亲自“体验”：他们将在操场上竞相建造铁路模型，一些学生被迫以更便宜的工资“工作”更长时间、更快。黄在本学年是一名中学老师，他希望他能让学生们了解华裔美国人如何为美国做出贡献，这是他在旧金山湾区长大的学生所没有得到的。 “我很早就种下了种子，”他说。 “这就是我所希望的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K) And, despite setbacks, the tide may finally be turning. California legislators passed a bill last year that will bring ethnic studies to all its public high schools. Some school districts, including San Francisco and Los Angeles, already offer ethnic studies at its high schools. High schools in Portland, Chicago, and elsewhere have either implemented or will soon introduce ethnic studies classes. And, as more high schools begin teaching it, the door could crack open for middle schools, and, perhaps inevitably, elementary schools, to incorporate a truly more multicultural curriculum. Doing so will send an important message to the nation's youngest citizens: Whatever your race or ethnicity, you matter. Your history matters. Your story matters.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 而且，尽管遇到了挫折，潮流可能最终会扭转。加州立法者去年通过了一项法案，将把种族研究引入所有公立高中。包括旧金山和洛杉矶在内的一些学区已经在其高中提供种族研究。波特兰、芝加哥和其他地方的高中已经开设或即将开设种族研究课程。而且，随着越来越多的高中开始教授这种课程，中学以及小学（也许不可避免地）纳入真正更加多元文化的课程的大门可能会打开。这样做将向该国最年轻的公民传达一个重要信息：无论您的种族或民族如何，您都很重要。你的历史很重要。你的故事很重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. While cultural holidays are celebrated, the injustices experienced by Asian Americans are not exposed in elementary school classrooms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 虽然庆祝文化节日，但亚裔美国人所经历的不公正并没有在小学课堂上暴露出来。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Little information can be found about Chinese immigrants in the author's school library.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 在作者所在学校的图书馆里，关于中国移民的信息很少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. A middle school teacher is making a great effort to help students learn about the contributions made by
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 一位中学老师正在努力帮助学生了解老师所做的贡献

paragraphs.sourceText: Chinese immigrants to America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 中国移民到美国。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. No Asian Americans were included in the list of historical figures recommended for study in K-12 classrooms.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 推荐在 K-12 教室学习的历史人物名单中没有亚裔美国人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. There 1s an obvious lack of teachers with a multicultural perspective to meet the curriculum challenges in America.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 美国明显缺乏具有多元文化视角的教师来应对课程挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Students of ethnic backgrounds learn better from a multicultural curriculum.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 种族背景的学生可以从多元文化课程中学到更好的知识。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Now more and more high schools in America are including ethnic studies in their curriculums.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 现在美国越来越多的高中将种族研究纳入其课程中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. A study of some K-12 textbooks and teacher manuals showed that Asian Americans were inadequately and improperly represented in them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 对一些 K-12 教科书和教师手册的研究表明，亚裔美国人在其中的代表性不足且不恰当。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. When taking a class in college, the author realized that a lot of information about Asian Americans was left out of the textbooks he studied.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 在大学上课时，作者发现他学习的教科书中遗漏了很多有关亚裔美国人的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. An Asian-American studies professor placed greater emphasis on teacher training than on teachers' background.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 一位亚裔美国人研究教授更重视教师培训而不是教师背景。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When is cleaning walls a crime? When you're doing it to create art, obviously. A number of street artists around the world have started expressing themselves through a practice known as reverse graffiti （涂鸦）. They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses (高压水管）. Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. The UK's Paul Curtis, better known as Moose, operates around Leeds and London
paragraphs.translationZh: 什么时候清洁墙壁是犯罪？显然，当你这样做是为了创造艺术时。世界各地的许多街头艺术家已经开始通过一种被称为反向涂鸦的做法来表达自己。他们找到肮脏的表面，然后使用清洁刷或高压水管在上面涂上图像或信息。无论哪种方式，都是相同的原理：图像是通过清除污垢而形成的。每个艺术家都有自己的个人风格，但所有艺术家都有一个共同的目标：引起人们对我们城市污染的关注。英国的保罗·柯蒂斯（Paul Curtis），更广为人知的名字是穆斯（Moose），在利兹和伦敦附近开展业务

paragraphs.sourceText: and has been commissioned by a number of companies to make reverse graffiti advertisements.
paragraphs.translationZh: 并受多家公司委托制作反向涂鸦广告。

paragraphs.sourceText: Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. Made up of a series of white skulls (颅骨），the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet. "Every motorist sits in the comfort of their car, but they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment and consequently for themselves," says Orion.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2006 年，巴西艺术家 Alexandre Orion 通过清除污垢，将圣保罗的一条交通隧道变成了一幅令人惊叹的壁画。这幅画由一系列白色头骨组成，提醒司机他们的污染对地球造成的影响。“每个司机都坐在舒适的车里，但他们没有考虑他们的舒适对环境以及对他们自己的影响，”猎户座说。

paragraphs.sourceText: The anti-pollution message of the reverse graffiti artists confuses city authorities since the main argument against graffiti is that it spoils the appearance of both types of property: public and private. This was what Leeds City Council said about Moose's work: "Leeds residents want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods. We view this kind of advertising as environmental damage and will take strong action against it." Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again?
paragraphs.translationZh: 反向涂鸦艺术家的反污染信息让城市当局感到困惑，因为反对涂鸦的主要论点是它破坏了两种财产的外观：公共财产和私人财产。利兹市议会对穆斯的工作是这样评价的：“利兹居民希望生活在干净、有吸引力的社区。我们认为这种广告是对环境的破坏，并将采取强有力的行动予以打击。”穆斯被勒令“改正他的行为”。他该怎么做：让他清理过的所有财产再次变脏？

paragraphs.sourceText: As for the Brazilian artist's work, the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with. They had no other option but to clean the tunnel but only the parts Alexandre had already cleaned. The artist merely continued his campaign on the other side. The city officials then decided to take drastic action. They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo.
paragraphs.translationZh: 至于这位巴西艺术家的作品，当局很恼火，但找不到任何罪名。他们别无选择，只能清理隧道，但只清理亚历山大已经清理过的部分。这位艺术家只是在另一边继续他的活动。市政府官员随后决定采取严厉行动。他们不仅清理了整个隧道，还清理了圣保罗的每条隧道。

paragraphs.translationZh: 46.我们从反向涂鸦的段落中学到了什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 反向涂鸦艺术家尝试做什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 关于巴西艺术家 Alexandre Orion，我们了解什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision?
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 作者对利兹市议会的决定有何暗示？

paragraphs.sourceText: The practice of paying children an allowance became popular in America about 100 years ago. Nowadays, American kids on average receive about $ 800 per year in allowance. But the vast majority of
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约100年前，给孩子发放零用钱的做法在美国开始流行。如今，美国孩子平均每年领取约800美元的零用钱。但绝大多数

paragraphs.sourceText: American parents who pay allowance tie it to the completion of housework. Although many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children, a range of experts expressed concern that tying allowance very closely to chores may not be ideal. In fact, the way chores work in many households worldwide points to another way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国父母支付津贴与完成家务挂钩。尽管许多家长认为支付完成家务活的津贴对孩子有好处，但许多专家表示担心，将津贴与家务活紧密联系起来可能并不理想。事实上，世界上许多家庭的家务劳动方式表明了另一种方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Suniya Luthar, a psychologist, is against paying kids for chores. Luthar is not opposed to giving allowances, but she thinks it's important to establish that chores are done not because they will lead to payment, but because they keep the household running. Luthar's suggested approach to allowance is compatible with that of writer Ron Lieber, who advises that allowances be used as a means of showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about. Kids should do chores, he writes, "for the same reason adults do, because the chores need to be done, and not with the expectation of " compensat10n.
paragraphs.translationZh: 心理学家苏尼娅·卢塔尔 (Suniya Luthar) 反对付钱给孩子做家务。卢瑟并不反对发放津贴，但她认为重要的是要确定，做家务不是因为它们会带来报酬，而是因为它们能让家庭运转。卢瑟建议的零用钱方法与作家罗恩·利伯的方法一致，后者建议用零用钱来向孩子们展示如何在他们关心的事情上储蓄、给予和消费。他写道，孩子们应该做家务，“与成年人做家务的原因相同，因为家务需要完成，而不是期望”补偿。

paragraphs.sourceText: This argument has its critics, but considering the way chores are undertaken around the world may change people's thinking. Professor David Lancy of Utah State University has studied how families around the world handle chores. At about 18 months of age, Lancy says, most children become eager to help their parents, and in many cultures, they begin helping with housework at that age. They begin with very simple tasks, but their responsibilities gradually increase. And they do these tasks without payment. Lancy contrasts this with what happens in America. "We deny our children's bids to help until they are 6 or 7 years old," Lancy says, "when many have lost the desire to help and then try to motivate them with payment. The solution to this problem is not to try to use money as an incentive to do housework, but to get children involved in housework much earlier, when they actually want to do it. "
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种说法受到了批评，但考虑到世界各地做家务的方式可能会改变人们的想法。犹他州立大学的大卫·兰西教授研究了世界各地的家庭如何处理家务。兰西说，在大约 18 个月大时，大多数孩子都会渴望帮助父母，而且在许多文化中，他们在这个年龄就开始帮助做家务。他们从非常简单的任务开始，但他们的责任逐渐增加。他们做这些任务是没有报酬的。兰西将此与美国发生的情况进行了对比。兰西说：“我们会拒绝孩子们帮忙的请求，直到他们六七岁为止，那时许多人已经失去了帮忙的愿望，然后试图通过付费来激励他们。解决这个问题的方法不是试图用金钱作为做家务的激励，而是让孩子们更早地参与家务，当他们真正想做的时候。”
